text:
anya: Heads-up — bringing Hyperbloom-14B into onboarding. License text looks like it might block redistribution of derived weights after quantization. Copying the relevant line below.

sam: can you paste the exact clause?

anya: `License excerpt: "Use allowed for research and hosting; redistribution of derived weights (including quantized or otherwise transformed checkpoints) is prohibited except by express written permission; attribution required."`

michael: so quantized weights are probably "derived" — transforms count. that would block shipping any quantized files.

sam: Key product questions: 1) Is hosting via our Hosted API allowed? 2) Can Dedicated or Private customers run it via our managed images? 3) Can we provide a container image with quantized weights? if redistribution prohibited, #3 is a no.

jia: platform note — Private (BYO) installs where customer brings their own weights should be fine since we don't redistribute. Dedicated currently involves us storing weights in our infra — might be considered redistribution depending on wording.

sam: generally "hosting a service" != redistribution, but some licenses explicitly disallow public hosting or require additional grants. redistribution prohibition definitely blocks shipping weights in a container or marketplace bundle. attribution clauses mean we need UI/docs copy.

anya: on the bench, quantizing to int8 + PTQ gave ~2.5x token throughput and small F1 regression. We want to move forward with latency wins but can't until legal clears the redistribution/hosting angle. any mitigations?

michael: two options: 1) ask upstream for a commercial/hosting license (ask for explicit permission to redistribute quantized derivatives), or 2) design a BYOW (bring-your-own-weights) path for Dedicated/Private customers and keep Hosted API off for now.

sam: agree. BYOW is safest short-term. For Hosted/Dedicated we'd need an explicit grant. i'll draft an outreach email template to upstream maintainers and loop in Partnerships.

anya: quick Q on attribution: clause says "must include model name and link to repo" — is in-app attribution (About page + API docs) sufficient? or do we need contractual language for enterprise customers?

sam: typical requirement: visible attribution in product docs or About page is fine for general users. for enterprise contracts we also add an attribution appendix to be conservative. i can draft standard copy for the console footer and docs.

legal-bot: Automated: ticket created in Legal queue (#legal-review). Priority: P2. Case ID: LR-2418.

jia: technical follow-up: if we implement BYOW, we need an ingest flow, checksum verification, and a minimal onboarding checklist (license attestation from customer, key rotation, storage TTL). i'll sketch a design and share a PR.

anya: OK — pausing hosted quant experiments until we get legal sign-off or upstream grant. thanks all :thumbsup:

sam: filing next steps: (a) i'll send outreach to upstream (template + ask for redistribution permission), (b) legal will confirm whether our "hosting" is allowed under current wording, (c) partnerships to engage if needed. expected ETA: 3-5 business days.

michael: in the meantime i'll run evals on the non-hosted BYOW flow so we have metrics ready.

anya: thanks team, marking this thread resolved for now.
